topic: understanding the concept of a step function or piecewise cost

easy.text: A parking garage charges $5 for the first hour, then $5 for each additional hour (or part of an hour). How much does 2.5 hours of parking cost?

options.feedback: Correct -- 2.5 hours requires rounding up to 3 full billed hours (first hour + 2 more), so 3×$5=$15.
This treats the cost as continuous/proportional, but the pricing is based on whole (rounded-up) hours, not fractional ones.
This only counts 2 billed hours, but 2.5 hours actually requires rounding up to 3 billed hours.
This only accounts for the first hour, ignoring the additional time parked.

medium.text: Using the same parking garage rule ($5 per hour or part of an hour), how much does exactly 4 hours of parking cost?

options.feedback: Correct -- exactly 4 full hours costs 4×$5=$20, with no partial hour needing to be rounded up.
This rounds up to 5 hours unnecessarily, when exactly 4 full hours requires no rounding.
This only counts 3 hours, undercounting the actual 4 hours parked.
This confuses the number of hours with the actual dollar cost.

hard.text: A shipping company charges $10 for packages up to 5 lbs, then an additional $3 for every additional pound (or part of a pound) beyond that. What is the cost to ship a 7.2 lb package?

options.feedback: Correct -- the first 5 lbs costs $10; the remaining 2.2 lbs rounds up to 3 billed additional pounds, costing 3×$3=$9, for a total of 10+9=19.
This treats the extra weight as continuous/proportional, but the pricing is based on whole (rounded-up) additional pounds, not fractional ones.
This only rounds up to 2 extra billed pounds, but 2.2 lbs actually requires rounding up to 3.
This overcounts the extra billed pounds beyond what's actually needed for 7.2 lbs.

easy.hard: Any partial unit of time or weight still counts as a full unit for billing purposes in this type of pricing structure.
easy.medium: Since any part of an hour counts as a full hour, round 2.5 up to the next whole hour.
easy.easy: Since any part of an hour counts as a full hour, round 2.5 up to 3.

medium.hard: Multiply the flat per-unit rate by the exact number of whole units used, when no rounding is needed.
medium.medium: Since it's exactly 4 whole hours, no rounding is needed -- just multiply by the rate.

hard.hard: Separate the base fee from the additional charge, rounding UP any partial additional unit to the next whole unit before multiplying by the per-unit rate.
hard.medium: Start with the base $10 for the first 5 lbs, then round the remaining weight up to the next whole pound before multiplying by $3.
hard.easy: Start with $10, then round 2.2 extra pounds up to 3, and multiply by $3, then add to the $10.
